recentItems.title: Race car driver saves competitor from burning wreckage
recentItems.description: British racer Ollie Millroy's Ferrari burst into flames during a China GT Championship race in Shanghai. Before emergency crews arrived, rival Dutch racer Loek Hartog charged into the fireball, pulled him from the wreck and, according to Millroy, saved his life.

recentItems.title: Prince Harry, Meghan remain non-working royals after return to the UK
recentItems.description: Britain’s King Charles III has said the Duke and Duchess of Sussex remain non-working royals and will not be carrying out official engagements on behalf of the Crown, following their return to the United Kingdom after six years in the United States. CNN’s Anna Stewart reports.

recentItems.title: Canada retaliatory tariffs loom as Ottawa moves to rename Trump Ave
recentItems.description:
On September 8, Canada is set to enact tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on over 700 American goods in an effort to match US tariffs dollar for dollar, Canadian officials announced on Tuesday.

Notably, Canada is doubling its duties on US steel and aluminum to 50%, in line with the 50% tariffs the US had already imposed on Canadian steel and aluminum before the latest round of US tariffs. Canadian officials framed the move as a means of protecting Canadian manufacturing.

recentItems.title: Mom convicted of misdemeanor after son walks alone in gated community
recentItems.description:
A Virginia mother was convicted of misdemeanor for allowing her five-year-old son to walk alone to collect feathers in their gated community. She’s now on the Virginia Child Abuse and Neglect Central Registry for the next seven years. 

The legal fallout has sparked intense debate over parenting rights and government oversight. CNN has reached out to James City County Child Protective Services and Police Department for comment.
